column1: # Ground truth for the BPM evaluation harness.
# Audio is never committed. This file points at a local directory, given to the
# harness with --corpus, and records enough to prove that a later run measured
# the same audio as an earlier one.
#   scripts/bpm-eval.sh --corpus ~/Music/bpm-corpus
# Tab separated. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
#   relative_path   Relative to the corpus root, so this file works on any
#                   machine that has the audio.
#   sha256          Of the file. Leave empty to skip the check while you are
#                   still assembling the corpus; fill it in with
#                   `sha256sum <file>` once the entry is settled. A mismatch is
#                   reported and the track is skipped, because measuring
#                   different audio under the same name makes two runs
#                   incomparable without saying so.
#   truth_bpm       The real tempo.
#   truth_source    One of:
#                     tapped     tapped out by hand. The good stuff.
#                     tag        the file's own BPM tag. Only as good as
#                                whatever wrote it, and note that a tag written
#                                by another detector means grading a detector
#                                against a detector.
#                     published  stated by the release, label or dataset.
#   notes           Free text. Worth using for anything that makes a track hard:
#                   tempo changes, rubato, a long ambient intro, live drumming.
# There are no rows yet. Until there are, the harness runs on its synthetic
# corpus alone, which is easier than real music and so reports an optimistic
# figure. A filled-in copy with real paths belongs in docs/private/, which is
# not published.
# relative_path
